# didactum/lessons — Open Ecosystem Guide (`didactum: 1`)

> Open lessons, perspectives, Teaching Styles, translations, 3D logical assets, and facet aliases for Didactum (`didactum: 1`). Every contribution is validated offline in `<1s` and published at its content address immediately on merge.

Read this file end-to-end before authoring a PR. It contains every rule an AI agent or human contributor needs to ship cleanly in one shot.

---

## 1. Core Architecture (`didactum: 1`)

### Directory-is-the-Registry & `id != path`
- **Zero central index files.** There is no central registry JSON to edit or cause merge conflicts. Putting a valid `.json`, `.yaml`/`.yml`, or `.score` artifact in a directory registers it.
- **`id != path`.** Every artifact's canonical identity is its `id` field (`@<namespace>/<slug>` or maintainer-only `didactum/<slug>`), never its file path. Moving or reorganizing files preserves identity and composition links.
- **Namespace trust binding:**
  - Community PRs must bind `<namespace>` to the contributor's immutable GitHub numeric account ID (`@gh-<github_actor_id>/<slug>` or `@<github_actor_id>/<slug>`) or a mapped contributor handle.
  - `didactum/*` is maintainer-only and rejected on community PRs.

### Repo-Level License + DCO (`Signed-off-by:`)
- This repository is licensed under **CC-BY-4.0** at the repo level (`LICENSE`).
- **Never** add a `license` field to `lesson`, `overlay`, `alias`, `binding`, `concept`, or `course` artifacts (`DID-E003`). Only `kind: asset` may carry an explicit third-party `license`.
- Every commit in a PR must include a **Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO)** trailer (`git commit -s`):
  `Signed-off-by: Your Name <you@example.com>`

### 4-Tier Medallion Trust System (`Bronze → Silver → Gold → Platinum`)
1. **Bronze** — New community PRs that pass the offline validator and safety guards publish **immediately at Bronze** by direct URL / content digest (`sha256:...`). Bronze artifacts play safely in sandboxed views (with untrusted prompt fencing) and stay out of default K–12 seeded rotation.
2. **Silver** — Passes deterministic composition, peer-conflict, and `TRUTH_CHECKS` verification.
3. **Gold** — Verified via maintainer review and/or positive randomized learner-outcome lift.
4. **Platinum** — Flagship curriculum artifacts with full verification and proven learner-outcome lift.

---

## 2. Hard Invariants (What the Validator Enforces)

- `didactum: 1` (integer `1`, never `"1.0"`).
- **No authored `version` field** (`DID-E002`). Revisions are immutable `sha256` content digests.
- **No per-artifact `license`** except on `kind: asset` (`DID-E003`).
- **Offline `kind_schema` only** (`DID-E004`), e.g. `didactum.kind/lesson@3`, `didactum.kind/overlay@1`, `didactum.kind/asset@1`, `didactum.kind/alias@1`. Live `http://` or `https://` URLs are forbidden.
- **Explicit BCP-47 `lang`** required on all text-bearing artifacts (`en`, `es-MX`, `zh-Hans`, ...; no implicit default) (`DID-E005`).
- **Zero raw `[x, y]` coordinates** in core lessons. Author in `.score` (declarative `CHALK:` / scene macros like `enclosure`, `right-triangle`, `area-grid`, `balance-scale`) or compiled AST `#node` scenes (`chalk_2d`, `mesh_3d`, `camera_3d`, `clip_plane`, `audio`, `passage`, `sim`).
- **No real-human voice or face biometrics** (`DID-E006`): `biometric_likeness: false` required on `kind: asset`; voice clones, face weights, and speaker embeddings are strictly rejected.
- **No binary blobs or executable code in git** (`DID-E017`, `DID-E018`): files `> 100 KB` and binary extensions (`.glb`, `.png`, `.wav`, `.mp3`, `.m4a`, etc.) are rejected; commit metadata-only `kind: asset` artifacts instead.
- **Zero vendor coupling**: never reference specific third-party avatar/video vendors.

---

## 3. All Open Composable Facets

Bundled offline schemas live in `schema/didactum-v1/`:
- `schema/didactum-v1/envelope.v1.json`
- `schema/didactum-v1/lesson.v3.json`
- `schema/didactum-v1/overlay.v1.json`
- `schema/didactum-v1/asset.v1.json`

### A. Core Lessons (`kind: lesson`, `.score` or compiled AST)
See `examples/river-pen-core.json` for a complete valid artifact.
- Declares `teaches: ["concept:<slug>"]`, `prereqs: ["concept:<slug>"]`, `params`, parsed `truth_checks` (`forall`/`exists` bounded non-Turing expressions), and `chapters` -> `beats` -> `lines` + `#node` scenes.
- Each beat sets `driver`: `"voice"`, `"learner"`, `"asset:<id>"`, or `"timer:<ms>"`.
- Answers, transfer keys, and rubrics use `visibility: "host-only"` and `frozen: true` (stripped by default-deny from learner views).
- Line mutability classes: `free`, `numeric-locked`, `frozen`.

Example `.score` format (zero raw coordinates):

```score
ID: @gh-12345678/river-pen-intro
LANG: en
TEACHES: concept:quadratic-optimization
PREREQS: concept:area-of-rectangle
PARAM: fence=120
PARAM: max_area=1800
TRUTH_CHECK: forall x in 0..60: x * (fence - 2 * x) <= max_area
HOST: transfer_answer=5000
TITLE: Maximize a River Pasture
SLUG: river-pen-intro
SUBJECT: math
GRADE: 9-12
CONCEPT: quadratic-optimization
PROBLEM: Enclose maximum area with 120 m of fence along a straight river.
ANSWER: 30 m by 60 m

## Sketch the river border
SAY: Imagine fencing a pasture where a straight river forms one side.
CHALK PIN: enclosure boundary=river left="x" back="120 - 2x" right="x" inside="A = x(120 - 2x)" as pen
```

### B. Perspectives & Locales (`kind: overlay`, `didactum.kind/overlay@1`)
- **Perspectives** (`astronomy`, `fantasy`, `sports`, `cooking`, ...) reframe contexts/analogies via the **7 closed ops**:
  `say.replace`, `say.aside(before|after)`, `say.direct`, `node.set`, `chapter.replace`, `param.set`, `meta.set`.
- **Locales** require explicit BCP-47 `lang` (`es-MX`, `fr`, `ja`, ...). When targeting `numeric-locked` lines with `say.replace`, the canonical numeral multiset must match the core line (`DID-E011`).

### C. Open Composable Teaching Styles (`kind: overlay`, `role: style`)
See `examples/history-humor-style.overlay.json` for a complete valid artifact.
- Composable dimensions: `tone` (`warm`, `deadpan`, `grumpy`, `brisk`, `calm`, ...), `textures` (`dry-humor`, `history-rich`, `socratic-probe`, `analogy-heavy`, ...), and `pacing` (`measured`, `brisk`, `rapid-drill`, ...).
- **Math truth is locked; rhetorical texture is open.** Style overlays CANNOT rewrite `numeric-locked` or `frozen` math lines (`DID-E011`, `DID-E010`). Instead, they enrich teaching with:
  - **Number-free `say.aside(before|after)`**: historical origin, dry humor, or Socratic nudges containing zero digits or number words (`DID-E012`).
  - **`say.direct`**: voice/delivery direction (`tone`, `pace`, `emphasis`).
- Pin `base` to `<core-id>@sha256:<64-hex>` so composition is digest-verified.

```yaml
didactum: 1
id: "@gh-12345678/socratic-astronomy-style"
kind: overlay
kind_schema: didactum.kind/overlay@1
lang: en
base: "@teetra/river-pen@sha256:8ade776a2e7d4732ac40d72120b10b99d6b239bf1c2324a2233a6b8226037615"
role: style
targets:
  tone: warm
  texture: socratic-probe
payload:
  role: style
  ops:
    - op: say.aside(before)
      address: "#b1.hook"
      text: "Before drawing a single equation, picture which side of the field needs no fence at all."
    - op: say.direct
      address: "#b1.eq"
      tone: warm
      pace: measured
```

### D. 3D Logical Assets (`kind: asset`, `didactum.kind/asset@1`)
See `examples/conic-3d.asset.json`.
- Metadata only in git (never commit `.glb` binaries).
- 3D conventions: **glTF 2.0**, **`+Y` up**, **right-handed**, units in **metres**.
- Requires `biometric_likeness: false`, `payload.asset_kind` (`gltf`, `image`, `svg`, `audio`, `diagram`, `sim-bundle`, `avatar-synthetic`, `voice-synthetic`), `payload.media_type`, `payload.sha256`, `payload.bytes`, and an explicit third-party `license` (`CC-BY-4.0`, `MIT`, etc.).

### E. Facet Aliases / Splits (`kind: alias`, `didactum.kind/alias@1`)
See `examples/teacher-split.alias.json`.
- Splits one legacy or composite facet (`from: "teacher:historian-wit"`) into multiple independent facets (`to: {tone: "deadpan", texture: "history-rich", pacing: "measured"}`) with cycle detection (`DID-E015`).

---

## 4. Fast `<1s` Local Validator & `fix: [ops]` Self-Repair Loop

Run the offline validator on any `.json`, `.yaml`/`.yml`, `.score`, or legacy `lessons/*.json` file:

```bash
python3 scripts/didactum_validate.py examples/ --json
```

Validate everything (legacy `lessons/` + `didactum: 1` artifacts + blob/executable checks):

```bash
python3 scripts/didactum_validate.py lessons examples --check-blobs --json
```

### Locked Machine-Readable Diagnostic Envelope
Every error or warning returns:

```text
{
  "code": "DID-E012",
  "severity": "error",
  "artifact": "@gh-12345678/my-style",
  "address": "#b1.hook",
  "pointer": "/payload/ops/0",
  "message": "say.aside must be number-free; found numeric quantity in '...'.",
  "fix": [
    { "op": "say.aside", "position": "after", "address": "#b1.hook", "text": "..." }
  ]
}
```

### Agent Self-Repair Loop
1. Run `python3 scripts/didactum_validate.py <your-file> --json`.
2. If `"ok": false`, read `diagnostics[]`.
3. For every diagnostic with a non-empty `fix` array, apply the suggested op (`meta.set`, `say.aside`, `say.replace`, `say.direct`, `node.set`, `param.set`, `chapter.replace`) at `address` / `pointer`.
4. Re-run `python3 scripts/didactum_validate.py <your-file> --json` until `"ok": true` and 0 errors (`<1s`).
5. Commit with `git commit -s` (DCO `Signed-off-by:`) and open your PR.

---

## 5. Legacy `lesson-package.v2.json` Compatibility

Existing lessons under `lessons/` use `schema/lesson-package.v2.json` and remain 100% supported. Both `python3 scripts/didactum_validate.py` and `python3 scripts/validate_lesson.py` validate them seamlessly. Reference shape:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "id": "community.same-denominator-fractions",
  "slug": "same-denominator-fractions",
  "metadata": {
    "subject": "math",
    "topic": "Adding fractions with the same bottom number",
    "concept_slugs": ["adding-fractions-like-denominators"],
    "grade_band": "3-5",
    "grade": 4,
    "language": "en",
    "authors": ["Your name or your agent's name"],
    "license": "CC-BY-4.0",
    "never_verbatim_verified": true
  },
  "problem": {
    "statement": "Ana ate 2/7 of a pizza and Ben ate 3/7 of it. What fraction of the pizza did they eat together?",
    "givens": ["Ana ate 2/7", "Ben ate 3/7"],
    "unknown": "the fraction eaten together",
    "assessment": {"answer": "5/7"}
  },
  "chapters": [
    {
      "id": "c1", "role": "why", "title": "Sharing one pizza",
      "beats": [
        {
          "id": "b1",
          "narration": {"text": "When pieces are the same size, you can just count them.", "intent": "pose"},
          "board": {
            "title": "Same-size pieces",
            "draw": [
              {"op": "circle", "c": [50, 36], "r": 22, "dur": 600},
              {"op": "line", "from": [50, 14], "to": [50, 58], "dur": 300},
              {"op": "line", "from": [28, 36], "to": [72, 36], "dur": 300}
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "c2", "role": "how", "title": "Count the slices",
      "beats": [
        {
          "id": "b2",
          "narration": {"text": "One fifth and two fifths make three fifths. The bottom number stays the same."},
          "board": {
            "title": "Add the tops",
            "lines": ["$\\frac{1}{5} + \\frac{2}{5} = \\frac{3}{5}$", "bottom stays 5"],
            "draw": [
              {"op": "polygon", "pts": [[10, 50], [90, 50], [90, 60], [10, 60]], "dur": 500},
              {"op": "line", "from": [26, 50], "to": [26, 60], "dur": 100},
              {"op": "line", "from": [42, 50], "to": [42, 60], "dur": 100},
              {"op": "line", "from": [58, 50], "to": [58, 60], "dur": 100},
              {"op": "line", "from": [74, 50], "to": [74, 60], "dur": 100},
              {"op": "label", "at": [34, 46], "text": "3 of 5", "size": 4}
            ]
          },
          "checkin": {
            "prompt": "What happens to the bottom number?",
            "choices": ["It stays the same", "We add it too"],
            "branches": {
              "It stays the same": "Yes. The slices are still fifths.",
              "We add it too": "The slices do not change size, so they are still fifths."
            }
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "b3",
          "narration": {"text": "Now add the tops of your two fractions and keep the bottom.", "intent": "celebrate"},
          "board": {
            "title": "Your turn",
            "lines": ["add the tops", "keep the bottom"],
            "draw": [{"op": "arrow", "from": [30, 40], "to": [70, 40], "dur": 400}]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
